item.p: The present Final Award is rendered in the context of a dispute between Premium Petroleum Services Corp. (Panama) as Claimant; Superior Energy Services Colombia, S.A.S. (Colombia) and Superior Energy Services, Inc. (U.S.A.) as Respondents; and Víctor Augusto Palacio Gaitán (Colombia) and María Eugenia Hernández Rojas (Colombia) as Additional Parties, concerning the Share Purchase Agreement executed on March 1, 2013.

The core of the present dispute revolves around alleged breaches of the SPA that each party asserts against the other party. Claimant seeks payment of the balance of the purchase price agreed under the Share Purchase Agreement amounting to US$ 1,250,000 plus interest and costs. Respondents, in turn, (i) raised jurisdictional objections with respect to Superior Energy Services Colombia, S.A.S.; (ii) requested dismissal of Claimant’s claims on grounds that they rightfully withheld the balance of the purchase price due to the Additional Parties’ breaches of the SPA; and (ii) filed counterclaims seeking an order for Claimant to pay damages, interest, and costs.

“10.2 Choice of Law/Dispute Resolution.
(a)
This Agreement shall be construed, interpreted and the rights of the parties determined in accordance with the laws of Colombia.
(b)
The parties agree that any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of, relating to or in connection with this Agreement, including, without limitation, any dispute regarding its validity or termination, or the performance or breach thereof, shall be finally settled by international arbitration administered by the International Chamber of Commerce in accordance with the International Chamber of Commerce’s rules of arbitration in effect at the time of the arbitration, except as they may be modified herein or by agreement of the parties. The place of arbitration shall be New York and the proceedings shall be conducted in English language. The arbitral tribunal shall be composed of three arbitrators. Each party shall appoint one arbitrator. The two arbitrators so appointed shall appoint the presiding arbitrator. If the two arbitrators to be appointed by the parties fail to agree upon a third arbitrator within thirty (30) days of the appointment of the second arbitrator, the third arbitrator shall be appointed by the International Court of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce. If a party neglects to appoint its arbitrator within thirty (30) days of the appointment of the other party’s arbitrator, then two arbitrators shall be appointed by the International Court of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce. Each of the arbitrators shall be and remain impartial and independent of the parties involved in the arbitration. The award rendered by the arbitrators shall be final and binding on the parties (to the extent they may validly so agree, the parties hereby exclude any right of appeal to any court of the arbitration or concerning the arbitral award). Notwithstanding the foregoing, any party may seek a preliminary injunction or other preliminary judicial relief if, in its reasonable, good faith judgment, such action is necessary to avoid irreparable damage. Despite such action, such party shall continue to participate in good faith in the procedures specified in this Section 10.2. All applicable statutes of limitations shall be tolled while the procedures specified in this Section 10.2 are pending, and the parties shall take any and all actions required to effectuate such tolling.”

On January 8, 2016, Claimant filed the Request for Arbitration (the “Request for Arbitration”) against Respondents. By a letter dated January 11, 2016, the Secretariat of the International Court of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce (the “Secretariat”) acknowledged receipt of Claimant’s Request for Arbitration.

On January 19, 2016, the Secretariat (i) notified Respondents of Claimant’s Request for Arbitration and informed that, pursuant to Article 5(1) of the ICC Rules, the Answer to the Request for Arbitration (the “Answer to Request for Arbitration”) was due 30 days after the receipt of the Request for Arbitration; and (ii) invited Respondents to send their comments regarding the selection of arbitrators within 30 days from the date Respondent received the Request for Arbitration.

On February 11, 2016, the Secretariat informed the Parties that (i) pursuant to Article 5(1) of the ICC Rules, the time limit for Respondents to submit their Answer to Request for Arbitration or any request for an extension of the time to submit their Answer to Request for Arbitration expired on February 29, 2016, for Superior Energy and on February 19, 2016, for Superior Colombia; (ii) that within the time limit granted, comments regarding the selection of the arbitrators were expected; and (iii) that within the same time limit, comments about the place of arbitration were also expected.
On February 18, 2016, Respondents requested an extension of time to file the Answer to Request of Arbitration.

On February 22, 2016, the Secretariat acknowledged Respondents’ request and granted until March 21, 2016 to (i) submit their Answer to Request for Arbitration and (ii) provide comments to the selection of the arbitrators and the place of arbitration.

Respondents submitted their Answer to Request for Arbitration on March 18, 2016, which also contained their Counterclaims (the “Counterclaims’) and the Request for Joinder of the Additional Parties (the “Request for Joinder”).

On April 5, 2016, the Secretariat acknowledged receipt of (i) Respondents’ Answer to Request for Arbitration, Counterclaims and Request for Joinder dated March 18, 2016, and (ii) the filing fee, which was credited to Respondents’ share of the advance on costs. The Secretariat also informed that (i) Claimant’s Reply was due on May 5, 2016; (ii) Claimant was invited to present comments on Respondents’ request to provide the Parties 30 days following the submission of the Answer to Request for Arbitration to jointly nominate the three arbitrators until April 12, 2016; (iii) the Arbitral Tribunal would decide any matter of jurisdiction or whether the claims may be determined together, after providing the Parties the opportunity to comment, pursuant to Article 6(3) of the ICC Rules; (iv) the Additional Parties were invited to present their comments on New York, New York (U.S.A.) as the place of arbitration, as agreed by Claimant and Respondents; and (v) the Patties wete invited to present their comments regarding the case caption of the file.

On the same date, the Secretariat notified the Additional Parties of Respondents’ Request for Joinder and informed that, pursuant to Article 7(4) of the ICC Rules, the Answer to the Request for Joinder was due 30 days after the receipt of the Request.

By letter dated April 12, 2016, Respondents clarified that (i) Superior Energy was the sole Counter-Claimant in this arbitration; (ii) only Superior Energy requested that the Additional Parties be joined to this arbitration; and (ii) accordingly, the Counterclaims and relief sought under the Answer, Counterclaims and Request for Joinder were jointly directed to Claimant and the Additional Parties.

On May 6, 2016, the Secretariat acknowledged receipt of Claimant’s and the Additional Parties’ correspondence dated May 5, 2016, enclosing an electronic copy of their Reply to Counterclaims and Answer of Additional Patties (the “Reply to Counterclaims and Answer of Additional Parties”).

On June 7, 2016, the Secretariat (i) acknowledged receipt of Claimants’ and the Additional Parties and Respondents’ correspondence dated June 6 and 7, 2016, regarding the constitution of the Arbitral Tribunal; and (ii) granted an extension until June 9, 2016, for the Parties to agree on the constitution of the Arbitral Tribunal.

On June 13, 2016, the Secretariat (i) acknowledged receipt of the Parties’ correspondence dated June 9, 2016, regarding the constitution of the Arbitral Tribunal; and (ii) granted an extension until July 12, 2016, for the Parties to constitute the Arbitral Tribunal.

On July 12, 2016, the Claimant and the Additional Parties jointly nominated Hunter T. Carter as co-arbitrator. On the same date, Respondents jointly nominated José Emilio Nunes Pinto as co-arbitrator.

On July 13, 2016, the Secretariat (i) acknowledged the Parties’ Second Amendment to Share Purchase Agreement; (ii) invited the prospective arbitrators to complete Statements of Acceptance, Availability, Impartiality and Independence; and (iii) informed the co-arbitrators that they had 30 days from their confirmation or appointment to nominate the President pursuant to Article 12(5).

On July 19, 2016, the Secretariat sent the Parties a copy of Hunter T. Carter’s Statement of Acceptance, Availability, Impartiality and Independence.

Carter as co-arbitrator upon Claimant’s and Additional Parties’ joint nomination; (ii) confirmed José Emilio Nunes Pinto as co-arbitrator upon Respondents’ joint nomination; (iii) invited the co-arbitrators to nominate the President of the Arbitral Tribunal by August 25, 2016; and (iv) informed that the provisional advance had been fully paid.

title.bd: TERMS OF REFERENCE AND PROCEDURAL ORDERS

item.p: On August 31, 2016, the President of the Arbitral Tribunal sent the first communication to the Parties, (i) requesting them to send, no later than September 12, 2016, a brief summary of their claims, defenses, and counterclaims as well as the relief sought; (ii) informing them that upon receipt of their comments, the Arbitral Tribunal would circulate a draft of the Terms of Reference and (iii) inviting them to confirm their availability to hold the Case Management Conference (the “Preliminary Conference”) under Article 24 of the ICC Rules via telephone conference call on September 23, 2016, at 10:00 EST (Eastern Standard Time).

By letter dated September 9, 2016, Respondents informed the Arbitral Tribunal that the Patties agreed to suspend the arbitral proceedings for a period of 45 days, which could be extended by the Parties’ mutual agreement, (the “First Suspension Period”) for the purpose of trying to settle their disputes through mediation in Colombia. The First Suspension Period was to expire on October 24, 2016.
By letter dated October 25, 2016, the Secretariat extended the limit for establishing the Terms of Reference until December 30, 2016.
On November 3, 2016, the Arbitral Tribunal invited the Parties to report the status of the mediation and whether they expected to reactivate the arbitral proceedings.

By letter dated November 8, 2016, Respondents informed the Arbitral Tribunal that the Parties were unable to teach an agreement in the mediation in Colombia and that they would resume contact with Claimant and Additional Parties to discuss procedural matters and inform the result of those discussions to the Tribunal in order to complete Terms of Reference and Procedural Order N° 1.

On November 15, 2016, the Arbitral Tribunal (i) invited the Parties to revert as promptly as possible the Arbitral Tribunal with their potential agreements/proposals regarding the conduction of the arbitral proceedings and (ii) reminded the Parties to provide a brief summary of their claims, defenses, and counterclaims as well as the relief sought no later than November 22, 2016.

On November 17, 2016, Respondents requested the Arbitral Tribunal to extend the deadline for the submission by the Parties of the summary of claims, defenses and counterclaims and the relief sought, to December 1, 2016. On the same date Claimant and Additional Parties confirmed the request for the extension of the deadline.

On November 19, 2016, the Arbitral Tribunal (i) granted the extension to submit the Parties’ summaries of claims, defenses and counterclaims and the reliefs sought, until December 1, 2016, and (ii) invited the Parties to make their best efforts to report within the same deadline the existence of any agreement on procedural matters.

By communications dated November 30 and December 1, 2016, the Parties informed the Arbitral Tribunal that they had agreed to suspend the arbitral proceeding for an additional period of two weeks, until December 16, 2016, for the purpose of trying to settle their disputes (the “Second Suspension Period”).

By letter dated on December 19, 2016, Respondents informed the Arbitral Tribunal that the Parties were unable to resolve their disputes during the Second Suspension Period. By communication of the same date, Claimant confirmed that the Parties did not teach an agreement.

On the same date, the Arbitral Tribunal acknowledged the communication or the parties and invited them to (i) submit their summaries of claims, defenses and counterclaims and the reliefs sought and (ii) make their best efforts to report any agreement on procedural matters no later than December 27, 2016.

On December 20, 2016, Respondents informed the Arbitral Tribunal that the firm BakerHostetler would be acting as co-counsel for Respondents in this arbitration and requested them to be included in the forthcoming correspondence.

On December 27, 2016, the Parties sent a negotiated draft of the Procedural Order N°1 for the Arbitral Tribunal’s consideration with the accepted points and the areas of disagreement. They informed the Tribunal that each patty would send a separated letter explaining the reasoning for their version of the disputed items.

On the same date, Claimant and Additional Parties sent to the Arbitral Tribunal their (i) summary of claims, defenses and counterclaims and the relief sought and (ii) position as to the draft Procedural Order N° 1. Respondents sent their summary for Terms of Reference and position for Procedural Order N° 1 by letter dated December 28, 2016.

On January 8, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal sent to the Parties the revised draft of the Terms of Reference and invited the Parties to (i) grant their approval or give comments no later than January 13, 2017, and (ii) hold the Case Management Conference Call on January 10 or 11, 2017. Upon request by the Parties, the Case Management Conference Call ultimately took place on January 16, 2017.
On January 13, 2017, the Parties sent to the Arbitral Tribunal their comments to the draft of the Terms of Reference proposed by the Arbitral Tribunal.

On January 20, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal sent to the Parties the revised Terms of Reference in which the Tribunal incorporated most of the Parties’ comments and included two comments where the Tribunal preferred to maintain its initial position. The Arbitral Tribunal invited the Parties to confirm their agreement in order to provide instructions for its execution.

On January 23, 2017, Claimant and Additional Parties sent their comments regarding the revised draft of the Terms of Reference. Respondents also sent their comments to the revised draft of the Terms of Reference on January 26, 2017.

On January 26, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal confirmed the reception of the Parties’ comments and informed them that it would revert shortly with a final version for its execution. On the same date Claimant and Additional Parties sent to the Arbitral Tribunal further responses to Respondents’ comments to the draft of the Terms of Reference.

On January 27, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal sent the final version of the Terms of Reference and invited the Patties’ approval no later than January 31, 2017. The Parties confirmed that they agreed with the final version.
On January 31, 2017, the Parties and the Arbitral Tribunal executed the Terms of Reference.

On February 17, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal issued Procedural Order N° 1 and the Procedural Timetable in which the Tribunal decided certain disputed procedural matters and established the rules applicable to the conduct of the arbitration and the Procedural Timetable.

On the same date the Arbitral Tribunal also issued the Preliminary Decision on matters related to Procedural Order N° 1 and the Procedural Timetable. In a nutshell, the Arbitral Tribunal decided inter alia on Respondents’ request for depositions, the attendance of non-party witnesses at the evidentiary hearing, request for three rounds of direct examination, translation of documents, and production of documents.

On May 15, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal issued Procedural Order N° 2 in which decided on the Document Request submitted by the Parties and sent them the Tribunal’s decision to the Parties’ Redfern Schedules.
On June 28, 2017, the Arbitral Tribunal issued the Procedural Order N° 3, with the amended Procedural Timetable.
On July 20, 2017, issued the Procedural Order N° 4, with a new amended Procedural Timetable.

On October 10, 2017, the Tribunal issued the Procedural Order N° 5, in which decided on Respondents’ Request for depositions and other procedural issues such as document production of responsive documents.
On November 3, 2017, the Tribunal issued the Procedural Order N° 6, containing its decision on the organization of the evidentiary hearing.

According to the Procedural Timetable on Procedural Order N° 1, on March 17, 2017, Claimant and the Additional Parties filed their Memorial of Claim (“Claimant’s Memorial of Claim”) and Respondents filed their Memorial of Counterclaims (“Respondents’ Memorial of Counterclaim”).
